# Compacted Summary: Chapter 1 (Complete and Final – Updated 28)

## Setting and Time
- **Season/Period**: Spring through late August, then Christmas/New Year period of the first year; now nearly three weeks into the new year (1832)
- **Primary Location**: Middlemarch and surrounding areas (Lowick, the Grange, Freshitt, Mirecombe, Salwick, Wilhaven, Quenwick, Fenmere, Bryngate, Chalky Flats, Gulton, Highbury, Cheltenham, Tipton, Yoddrell's farm, Frick, Miremere, Salmere, Riverston, Quallingham, Halsell Wood, Loamford, Brassing, Stone Court, Coldcombe, St. Peter's Place, Lowick Gate, Shrubs, Dunholt, Yorkshire, Staveton)
- **Atmospheric Details**: Baker's boy frequently late; wind off water with salt and tar smell; dog barking periodically; bees in lavender behind parsonage; gulls quarreling over fish heads; carts with turnips; frost silvering hedges; road rutted and puddled after thaw; children chasing hoops down lane; bell for vespers ringing thinly; chalk sun on forge wall; smoke from chimneys lying flat over fields; light going early at end of August; starlit darkness; frosty air in late year
- **Secondary Characters/Background**: Ilrine Corrett ("Old Ilrine"), herbalist; Eldette Corrett, cooper; Thidrek Corrett, smith; Ridan Corrett, glazier; Jotho Corrett ("Jotho the Younger"); Aessa Hollwood, ferryman; Cotho Hollwood, mason; Halan Hollwood, shepherd; Ulvie Hollwood, weaver; Thiena Hollwood, glazier; Elnar Brackwood, weaver; Senelle Brackwood, ferryman; Jovus Brackwood ("Red Jovus"), miller; Madan Brackwood, scribe; Cotho Brackwood, shepherd; Tassa Brackwood, weaver; Colan Lindson, born at Quenwick; Islis Lindson, shepherd, born at Quenwick

## Main Characters

**Dorothea**
- Recently widowed; residing at Lowick Manor
- Strong admiration for Caleb Garth's work knowledge; hopes to improve land and build good cottages
- Final Grange encounter: Will declared best is over, would live like one who saw heaven in trance
- Mistakenly believed Will's words referred to Mrs. Lydgate; experienced certainty his conduct with Rosamond should be above suspicion
- Though thought she might be what Will cared for most, doubt overcame this; credited all to friendship and obstruction from Casaubon's codicil
- Saw Will with portfolio on road; felt pang leaving him behind; wished they could have been happy thinking of each other
- Forced to keep money under Casaubon's codicil that ought to have been Will's, causing distress
- **Bulstrode's Report**: Described by Bulstrode as "a woman of most munificent disposition" in possession of funds she can well spare; has destined chief part of funds to another purpose; willing to consider taking Bulstrode's place in relation to Hospital; wishes ample time to mature thoughts; setting out on journey into Yorkshire with Sir James and Lady Chettam; her decision regarding Hospital contribution will depend on conclusions about land she is to see there

**Will Ladislaw**
- Spoke impetuously at Grange about what forbidden him by own pride and honor
- Passionate love for Dorothea which he forbade himself to utter; what kept him silent was that she was forced to keep money that ought to have been his
- After parting: certainty had much more bitterness; had no assurance she loved him
- Still at Middlemarch despite weeks since parting; frequenting Lydgate's household; warbling continually with Rosamond (scandal spreading per Mrs. Cadwallader)
- Raffles knows connection between Will and Bulstrode but deliberately conceals this as card to play
- Father was at Boulogne very ill; mother's family engaged in "respectable thieving line"; mother (Sarah) ran away after Archie Duncan rejected her
- Rejected Bulstrode's money; stated unblemished honor and unstained birth important; recognized stain through mother; refuses "ill-gotten money"; departed with determined quickness
- Wrote brief letter to Dorothea asking permission to call at Lowick

**Caleb Garth**
- Met Bulstrode regarding stable drainage at Stone Court
- Working with railroads: measured and valued outlying piece of land at Yoddrell's farm belonging to Lowick Manor; confronted laborers preparing to interfere with railroad agents
- Decided to take Fred Vincy on as assistant with desk-work and accounts; offered eighty pounds for first year, more after
- Character: ruled absolutely only on other people's behalf; on ninety-nine points Mrs. Garth decided, but on hundredth point Caleb was immovable ruler
- **Stone Court Opportunity**: Consulted by Bulstrode on farm management at Stone Court; advised against mere bailiff, recommended yearly letting of land, stock, and implements with proportionate share of proceeds; Bulstrode consulted, alluring idea occurred to Caleb—what if Fred Vincy could be placed at Stone Court under Caleb's management responsibility? Would be excellent schooling for Fred; Fred could make modest income while gaining business knowledge; Caleb mentioned notion to Mrs. Garth with such delight she could not dampen pleasure despite constant fear of his undertaking too much
- **Vision and Current Plans**: Pleased Fred's mind had run on Stone Court for years before Featherstone died; would be pretty turn of things for Fred to hold place in good industrious way after taking to business; Bulstrode might let him gradually buy stock; excited prospect of children being married by-and-by
- **Caleb Elated and Restraint**: So elated with hope of "neat turn" being given to things that without wifely scolding would have betrayed everything to Mary, wanting "to give the child comfort"; restrained himself and kept in strict privacy from Fred certain visits to Stone Court to look more thoroughly into state of land and stock, take preliminary estimate; more eager in these visits than probable speed of events required; stimulated by fatherly delight occupying mind with bit of probable happiness held in store like hidden birthday gift for Fred and Mary
- **Critical Moral Moment with Raffles**: Took up Raffles in his gig after Raffles got down from coach and was walking beyond turning from toll-house; Raffles had recognized Caleb from previous meeting at Stone Court with Bulstrode; Caleb saw Raffles was ill and provided shelter; felt right thing to carry him under shelter
- **Confrontation with Bulstrode**: When Bulstrode sent note to Lydgate at Hospital and prepared to ride to Stone Court, Caleb made firm declaration: must request Bulstrode put business into other hands; obliged to Bulstrode for handsome way of meeting him about Stone Court letting and other business but must give it up; spoke with firmness that was very gentle; Bulstrode seemed to cower under gentleness, face looking dried, eyes swerving away; Caleb felt deep pity for him but could use no pretexts to account for resolve
- **Moral Clarity on Raffles's Claims**: When Bulstrode attempted to dismiss Raffles as disreputable fellow spreading slander, Caleb stated: obliged to believe Raffles has told him truth; can't be happy working with Bulstrode or profiting by him; hurts his mind; must beg Bulstrode to seek another agent
- **Merciful Closing**: When Bulstrode tried further appeals, Caleb waved him off with merciful intention to spare pitiable man; said what Raffles told him will never pass from his lips unless something unknown forces it from him; acknowledged if Bulstrode led harmful life for gain and kept others out of their rights by deceit, he must repent—must want to go back but can't; that must be bitter thing; not for Caleb to make Bulstrode's life harder

**Mary Garth**
- Staying at Lowick Rectory with Miss Farebrother and Mrs. Farebrother
- Told Farebrother: "I have too strong a feeling for Fred to give him up for any one else"
- Upon Fred telling her of engagement with her father, touched keenly; scolded him for not seeing Farebrother's delicate feeling
- Earnestly desired to be clear she loved Fred best; determined to watch over her affections and constancy
- Currently telling stories to children at Lowick Parsonage (Rumpelstiltskin tale); Fred seated near her, watching with admiration

**Fred Vincy**
- Age four-and-twenty; son of Mr. Vincy; rejected Church vocation; took degree
- Encountered Caleb Garth at Yoddrell's farm; accepted eighty pounds for first year, more after
- Mr. Vincy responded with profound surprise and cutting disappointment; will keep no horse for Fred
- Casually mentioned to Rosamond what he heard about Casaubon's codicil mentioning Ladislaw
- Acknowledged debt to Caleb which will never be discharged
- At Lowick Parsonage: seated near Mary during storytelling; watching her with admiration
- Billiard room incident: encountered Lydgate gambling; felt shock; old opinion of Lydgate as prig reversed
- **Farebrother's Intervention and Warning**: Farebrother drew Fred aside at St. Botolph's; confessed temptation to let Fred go wrong; disclosed satisfaction of Fred's affections stands in way of his own; warned Mary's affection is "conditionally bound" and liable to change; claimed another man might win "firm place in her love as well as respect" through "companionship of ready sympathy" even over longest associations; Fred seized by uncomfortable chill; tone changed to encouraging; Farebrother spoke of returning to old intention and uttering warning; moment produced regenerating effect in Fred

**Mr. Lydgate**
- Doctor/physician; age nine-and-twenty
- **Financial Crisis Deepening**: Debt amounts to three hundred and eighty pounds at Brassing; creditor Mr. Dover holds bill of sale on furniture
- **Gambling Incident and Aftermath**: Played at billiard-table; won repeatedly but ended by losing four to five pounds overall; felt unmixed disgust next day; carried unpleasant vision, chewed disagreeable cud of regret
- **Contemplating Leaving Middlemarch**: Began familiarizing imagination with step unlike his remembered self—considering whether to quit Middlemarch without seeing beyond preface; questioned whether purchaser of practice forthcoming; against step was obstacle that Rosamond in poor lodging would not find life to save her from gloom
- **Hesitation About Bulstrode Approach**: Had created strong ideal obstacles to requesting considerable help from Bulstrode, whom he had often boasted of being totally independent of; thought Bulstrode's opinions contemptible
- **Bulstrode's Medical Consultation and Opportunity**: Note from Bulstrode requested Lydgate call at Bank; Bulstrode had hypochondriacal tendency showing; lacked sleep, dwelt on as sign of threatening insanity; moment when Bulstrode received medical opinion with comfort seemed to make communication of personal need easier than Lydgate's contemplation beforehand
- **At Bank Consultation—Hospital Crisis**: Bulstrode announced plans to cease personal share in Hospital management due to anticipated withdrawal from Middlemarch; will withdraw support except for supplying building expenses and large sums to successful working
- **Bulstrode's Plan**: Proposes amalgamation of New Hospital with Infirmary, making New Hospital special addition to elder institution with same directing board; states providential indications demand his renunciation, which he accepts
- **Dorothea as Potential Replacement Benefactor**: Bulstrode informed Lydgate that Dorothea may be certainly counted on as willing to increase contributions; she is setting out on journey into Yorkshire; conclusions about land she is to see may affect her power of contributing
- **Lydgate's Response**: Felt renewed hope about Hospital only made him more conscious of poisoning facts; effort for help must be made now and vigorously; spoke unwillingly as if biting objectionable leek
- **Direct Appeal for Financial Help**: Made direct statement to Bulstrode of his financial position; revealed he slipped into money difficulties with no way out unless someone trusts him and will advance thousand pounds without other security; has very little fortune when came to Middlemarch; marriage expenses much greater than expected; needs thousand pounds to clear himself
- **Bulstrode's Response**: Expressed grief though not surprise; regretted Lydgate's alliance with brother-in-law's family of prodigal habits; advised instead of involving himself in further obligations, Lydgate should become bankrupt

**Mr. Farebrother (Vicar)**
- Aware Lydgate is proud man; had been playing whist to satisfy mother
- **Intervention with Fred and Mary**: Left whist-table to speak with Lydgate, disclosing Lydgate had done him service by influencing him to stop playing for money; later approached Fred at billiard-table; confessed temptation to let Fred ruin himself; disclosed satisfaction of Fred's affections stands in way of his own; warned Mary's affection is "conditionally bound"; claimed another man might win firm place through companionship of ready sympathy; overcame temptation to act selfishly
- Watching Mary Garth with evident admiration while she tells Rumpelstiltskin tale

**Rosamond Lydgate (née Vincy)**
- Married to Lydgate; victorious obstinacy never wasting energy
- **Manipulation and Consequences**: Manipulated husband to go riding; accident at Halsell Wood led to loss of baby; regaining brilliant health
- Now possesses knowledge of Casaubon's codicil mentioning Will
- **Response to Debt Crisis**: When Lydgate proposed debt must be paid, fell like mortal chill; when presented with house-selling proposal, went to Mrs. Plymdale with congratulations instead; had secretly disobeyed by asking father for help; father said more likely to want help himself
- **Business Intervention**: Called on Mr. Borthrop Trumbull at his office; revoked Lydgate's order before New Year's Day party
- **Written to Sir Godwin with Refusal**: Had written requesting aid; awaited answer for nearly three weeks, every day disappointed; Sir Godwin refused all aid; stated wife should not write on business; cannot supply thousand pounds or half that sum
- **Response to Lydgate's Confrontation**: When Lydgate spoke of lack of openness and confidence, Rosamond refused to make admissions; expressed wish she had died with baby; her gentleness made words and tears omnipotent; does not identify her own acts according to strict classification

**Mr. Bulstrode**
- **Raffles Present Crisis**: Raffles currently at Bulstrode's home; told wife Raffles is wretched victim of vice; plans to drive him away by closed carriage next morning; provided wife with precautionary information
- **Terror of Exposure**: Tortured by fear lest Raffles be overheard in loud references to past facts; fears Mrs. Bulstrode might listen at door
- **Breaking Point with Raffles**: Raffles pushed torture too far; his hopelessly unmanageable behavior made Bulstrode feel strong defiance only resource left; after putting Raffles to bed, ordered closed carriage ready at half-past seven next morning; spent wretchedness in prayer
- **Visit to Raffles's Bedside**: Carried candle to bedside of Raffles in painful dream; stood silent hoping light would wake him gradually; watched shudderings and pantings for couple minutes; Raffles started with long half-stifled moan, stared in terror, trembled and gasped
- **After Raffles Leaves**: Returned to quiet home with no confidence he had secured more than respite; felt as if had loathsome dream, could not shake off images
- **Plans Deferred**: Arrangements for withdrawal had not gone farther than stage where he could recall them; continually deferred final steps; like man in danger of shipwreck, had clinging impression something would happen to hinder worst
- **Earlier Background**: Approximately fifteen months after Peter Featherstone's death, became proprietor of Stone Court through Joshua Rigg's land sale
- **Past Life**: Young banker's clerk; eminent though young member of Calvinistic dissenting church; became confidential accountant in Dunkirk's pawnbroker's business; magnificent profit from easy reception of goods without strict inquiry; perpetual self-justification; soul saturated with belief he did everything for God's sake; yet if could go back in youthful poverty would choose to be missionary
- **Later Years**: Wife died after five years; gradually withdrew capital but did not make sacrifices to end business, carried on for thirteen years before collapsing; became banker, Churchman, public benefactor
- **Current Crisis Nature**: When respectability lasted nearly thirty years, past had risen and immersed his thought; not coarse hypocrite consciously affecting beliefs; man whose desires stronger than theoretic beliefs, gradually explained gratification into satisfactory agreement with beliefs; poured out utterances of repentance; threatening Providence urged propitiation
- **Offer to Will and Reaction**: Wrote letter to Will; met with Will at Shrubs; Will asked if Bulstrode connected with pawnbroker's business; Bulstrode felt suddenly uncertain; could not tell lie; answered falteringly that Will conjectured rightly; offered five hundred pounds yearly during his life and proportional capital at death; when Will rejected money and departed with determined quickness, Bulstrode suffered violent reaction and wept like woman
- **Hypochondriacal Tendency and Medical Consultation**: Recently showing hypochondriacal tendency; lack of sleep dwelt on as sign of threatening insanity; requested Lydgate call at Bank for consultation
- **Plans for Change**: Change of plan and shifting of interest determined by severe experience since Raffles recognized Will Ladislaw; banker had in vain attempted act of restitution which might move Divine Providence to arrest painful consequences; contemplates temporary withdrawal from management of much business; thinking of changing residence for a time; probably will close or let 'The Shrubs' and take place near coast under advice as to salubrity; asked Lydgate if that would be measure he would recommend
- **Reaction to Caleb's Withdrawal**: When Caleb announced he must request Bulstrode put business into other hands because he believes Raffles told him truth about Bulstrode's harmful past life and deceit that kept others out of their rights, sharp certainty entered like stab into Bulstrode's soul; attempted to appeal to Caleb's faith and conscience, casting about for pleas that might be adapted to his hearer's mind; tried to dismiss Raffles as spreading slander; when Caleb remained firm and merciful, Bulstrode found no leverage; Caleb promised what Raffles told him will never pass from his lips unless something unknown forces it from him

**Mr. Raffles**
- Known to Bulstrode from twenty-five years prior; addresses him as "Nick"; claims to be visiting stepson Joshua Rigg
- Recalled name was "Ladislaw" and wrote it down in pocket-book; deliberately decided NOT to tell Bulstrode—holds secret knowledge of connection between Bulstrode and Ladislaw, intentionally concealing, treating as card to play
- Currently at Bulstrode's home; in painful dream; violent, loud, unmanageable
- Has revealed to Caleb Garth information about Bulstrode's harmful past life: that Bulstrode led harmful life for gain, kept others out of their rights by deceit to get more for himself
- Picked up by Caleb Garth in his gig after getting down from coach, walking beyond turning from toll-house; recognized Caleb from previous meeting at Stone Court; Caleb provided shelter due to seeing he was ill
